harness.question: Does the same agent, at the same budget, complete more real repository tasks with mind-mem than without it?
harness.differs_between_arms: One thing: a recalled-context prefix on the prompt. Asserted as memory.prompt == memory.memory_section + control.prompt.
harness.held_constant: Task, reported-issue statement, instruction footer, agent and argv, work tree (re-extracted from parent_sha between arms), environment (one shared object, not a comparison), token/step/wall ceilings, grading command.
harness.memory_gate: Structural, because this package ships no recall kill-switch: no MIND_MEM_* variable in the environment, no mm/mind-mem-* executable on PATH, a sandboxed HOME so no agent config or MCP server loads, and the seeded workspace placed outside the work tree.
harness.seeding: The memory arm is seeded only from commits reachable from parent_sha -- a git ancestry property, so the task's own commit and everything after it are unreachable by construction -- re-checked against memory_cutoff and scanned for the task commit id.
harness.grading: pytest only. A task passes iff pytest exits 0 and every fail_to_pass node passes. Editing any test voids the attempt.
harness.statistics: Paired McNemar exact, two-sided. Below 6 discordant pairs no split can reach p<=0.05; such a delta is noise.
harness.determinism: digest covers the scored record with every telemetry section removed, so no wall-clock value can move it.

memory_pointers_in_tree.why_this_is_not_a_leak: Same tree in both arms. mm / mind-mem-* are off PATH and HOME is a sandbox in both, so an agent that follows one of these finds nothing; they are named because an isolation claim should not be approximate.

agent.tail:
The failing tests referenced `mind_mem.governance_raft`, which didn't exist — the feature was missing entirely. I created **`src/mind_mem/governance_raft.py`** (the only file touched; no test or conftest changes), following the conventions of the sibling v4.0-prep module `event_fanout.py`:

- **`Proposal`** — frozen dataclass; `digest()` = SHA-256 over a canonical JSON encoding (sorted keys, fixed separators), so it's stable across calls and payload-sensitive.
- **`CommitResult`** — `committed` / `term` / `index` / `reason` (default `""`) / `digest` (default `b""`), matching the keyword construction used by the test's stub.
- **`LocalConsensusLog`** — single-node Raft semantics: always leader, term 1, monotonic 1-based indexes, immediate commit with `reason="local_immediate"`. Thread-safe; subscribers are notified outside the lock, and a raising handler is logged and skipped without blocking the commit.
- **`ConsensusLog`** — `runtime_checkable` protocol mirroring the interface clustered backends will implement.
- **Factory registry** — module-level `_factory` (the name the test fixture resets), `register_consensus_log()` / `create_consensus_log()` defaulting to the local log.
- **`replicate()`** — ordered per-proposal submission.
- **`sign_proposal` / `verify_proposal`** — HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical encoding with a 16-byte minimum secret: signing raises `ValueError` on short secrets, verification returns `False` (constant-time `hmac.compare_digest`) so attacker-supplied material never leaks length-check signals.
